text: I’ll model the fluid region as a rectangular box minus a 40 mm sphere centered at the origin. The streamwise axis is \(x\): the box runs from \(-0.20\) m to \(+0.60\) m, and from \(-0.20\) m to \(+0.20\) m in both transverse axes. I’ll use `blockMesh` for the coarse background grid and `snappyHexMesh` for sphere fitting, local refinement, and prism layers. First I’m creating and inspecting the metre-scale CAD geometry at coarse display resolution.

The first inspection exposed two measurement/construction mistakes rather than a valid geometry: I doubled an already full bounding-box diameter, and the translated box landed on the wrong side of the origin. I’m checking the installed `build123d` primitive and transform signatures before correcting the CAD; I will not mesh this invalid first draft.

`Box` is centered by default, so the correct box translation is its center at \(x=0.20\) m, not its minimum corner. I’m rebuilding the fluid solid with that correction and measuring diameter, extents, and volume again before generating any mesh files.
The corrected dimensions and volume now match exactly. I’m replacing the preview with a view of the corrected domain and sphere, including the upstream/downstream orientation.

Next I’m identifying the seven final fluid faces by their actual surface geometry and outward normal—not by bounding-box location. The two streamwise planar faces become inlet/outlet, the four transverse planar faces become one far-field patch, and the spherical face becomes the sphere patch.

The face inventory is exactly as expected: six planes and one spherical cavity, with the sphere area matching \(4\pi R^2\). I’ll now bind the named patches from surface type and face normal and export all four patch groups in one conformal tessellation.

For the coarse background mesh I’m choosing a 20 mm Cartesian cell: \(40\times20\times20=16{,}000\) cells before sphere refinement. This is intentionally coarse for topology validation. The outer boundaries are named directly in `blockMeshDict`; the sphere patch will be created by `snappyHexMesh`.

`blockMesh` correctly refused to run because an OpenFOAM case also requires `system/controlDict`. I’ll create the minimal mesh-only control file and recreate the background dictionary in the same accepted step, then rerun the coarse background mesh.

The coarse box mesh is valid at 16,000 cells. For the first fitted mesh I’ll refine the sphere surface to 5 mm nominal cells (8 cells across the diameter), add two distance-refinement bands, and request four prism layers on `sphere` only. Because no Reynolds number or target \(y^+\) was given, these layer dimensions are a geometric assumption for meshing validation rather than a flow-specific wall resolution.
I’ll now run the coarse fitted mesh in-place and inspect the mesher’s own cell and layer reports before deciding whether refinement or layer controls need adjustment.

This OpenFOAM build initializes finite-volume settings even for meshing, so `snappyHexMesh` also needs minimal `fvSchemes` and `fvSolution` files. I’m adding mesh-only defaults and then rerunning; the background mesh was not modified by the failed startup.

The mesher reached the snap phase and exposed a version-specific required quality-control entry (`errorReduction`). I’m adding the standard smoothing/error-reduction entries, restoring the pristine background mesh, and rerunning from the start so no partially written mesh is reused.

The coarse fitted mesh completed with 26,768 cells. All 200 sphere surface faces received all four requested prism layers, with 3.88 mm total geometric layer thickness. I’ll now run the binding `checkMesh` test and inspect patch topology and mesh quality.

`checkMesh` passes: one connected region, all four named patches present, maximum non-orthogonality 31.94°, maximum skewness 0.680, and positive cell volumes. I’m now looking at a center-plane cut to verify sphere removal, wake-side refinement, and the visible prism stack rather than relying only on statistics.

The coarse center plane confirms the correct external region, smooth local refinement, and a complete circumferential layer stack. For the final mesh I’ll increase the sphere to nominal 2.5 mm surface cells (16 across the diameter), use three graded refinement bands, and increase to five layers. I’m assuming a 0.20-cell final-layer thickness and 1.2 growth ratio because velocity, viscosity, Reynolds number, and target \(y^+\) were not specified.

The final mesh has 107,872 cells. All 744 sphere faces received all five layers, with 0.241 mm average near-wall layer thickness and 1.79 mm total thickness. I’ll rerun the binding mesh check on this final mesh and measure its actual extents from the generated points.

The final mesh passes `checkMesh` with maximum non-orthogonality 34.26°, maximum skewness 0.560, and one connected region. The streamwise extents are exact; transverse smoothing changed the far-field extent by at most 0.048 mm (0.024% of the specified half-width). I’m measuring the fitted sphere patch itself and producing the final center-plane view.

The final sphere patch measures 39.964–40.000 mm across the three axes, with mean point radius 19.989 mm; this is the expected small faceting error at 2.5 mm nominal surface resolution. The final view confirms graded refinement and the five-layer near-wall stack. I’ll perform a final artifact/script inventory before declaring the case complete.

The mesh artifacts are already present; `build.py` is assembled from accepted cells by the desk framework at completion rather than materialized during the live kernel session. I’ll verify the case files themselves, then run the completion checks.

Completed geometry and mesh:

- 40 mm CAD sphere centered at the origin.
- Domain: 5D upstream, 15D downstream, and 5D to each transverse side.
- Named patches: `inlet`, `outlet`, `farField`, `sphere`.
- Final mesh: 107,872 cells; 744 sphere faces.
- Sphere fitting: 39.964–40.000 mm measured diameters.
- Prism layers: 5/5 layers on 100% of sphere faces; 0.241 mm average near-wall thickness and 1.79 mm total thickness.
- `checkMesh`: passed; max non-orthogonality 34.26°, max skewness 0.560.

Assumptions: 20 mm background cells, 2.5 mm nominal sphere cells, three refinement bands at 40/80/120 mm, layer growth ratio 1.2, and final layer thickness 0.20 local cells. These are geometric mesh choices because no Reynolds number, wall \(y^+\), velocity, or fluid properties were specified. Snappy smoothing shifted transverse far-field extrema by at most 0.048 mm; streamwise extents remained exact. No flow-specific boundary-layer adequacy was checked.

The completion gate requires the external-region seed point to be recorded in the surface manifest, even though the same valid point is already in `snappyHexMeshDict`. I’ll re-export the same named patches with `location_in_mesh=(-0.10,0,0)` so the CAD manifest independently verifies that the retained region is outside the sphere and inside the domain.
The exporter supports this directly. I’m regenerating the conformal patch set unchanged, adding only the validated fluid seed point to its manifest.
The manifest now records the external-flow seed at \((-0.10,0,0)\) m, which lies inside the fluid box and 80 mm clear of the sphere surface. The geometry and mesh are otherwise unchanged.
